questions.answer:
# Kafka and Project Beacon's Event Streaming Layer

**No, Kafka is not being used for Project Beacon's event streaming layer.** The team considered adopting it but reversed that decision, and RabbitMQ remains in use.

## The Decision Reversal

On 2026-03-13, the team reversed its earlier decision to adopt Kafka for Project Beacon's event streaming layer. The reason was that latency benchmarks showed insufficient gains to justify the cost of migrating [Data: Sources (56); Entities (163, 161, 164); Relationships (316, 317, 326)].

## Why Kafka Was Rejected

The benchmarks compared Kafka's latency against RabbitMQ, which served as the baseline. They showed the improvement was too small to justify migration, and this was the stated reason for the reversal [Data: Entities (165); Relationships (320, 321, 322)]. The proposed migration would have moved the event streaming layer from RabbitMQ to Kafka, but it was cancelled because of its cost [Data: Entities (164); Relationships (323, 325, 326)].

## What Is Used Instead

Project Beacon's event streaming layer continues to use RabbitMQ, and the team has said it will keep doing so [Data: Entities (162); Relationships (314, 318)]. Kafka was considered for the project but not adopted [Data: Relationships (315, 319)].

## Caveat

The most recent record on this topic is dated 2026-03-13. The data tables contain nothing suggesting the decision was revisited after that date.
